mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC has drifted up from -10.0 at t-3w to -8.9 at t-0w, a slow reopening ramp rather than a reversal; extrapolating that positive slope makes the next 28-day mean higher than the last 28-day mean.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC weekly means -10.0, -9.3, -8.3, -8.9 over t-3w to t-0w
failure_condition: Next-28-day mean RETAIL_REC is at or below the prior 28-day mean of about -9.1, rejecting trend continuation.

mechanism_narrative: Joint deterioration in TRANSIT (-5.4 to -7.4) and WORKPLACES (-0.1 to -9.9) in the latest week marks a renewed commuter pullback; fewer workplace trips cut weekday discretionary footfall and drag RETAIL_REC down over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES and TRANSIT both fall week-on-week by more than 2 points
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES fell 9.8 points and TRANSIT fell 2.0 points between t-1w and t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises over the following 14 days despite joint WORKPLACES and TRANSIT week-on-week declines exceeding 2 points.

mechanism_narrative: A single-week WORKPLACES drop steeper than 5 points is the signature of a reinstated work-from-home directive, and the capacity limits attached to such directives propagate to retail-and-recreation within one week.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES fell from -0.1 at t-1w to -9.9 at t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC in week t+1 exceeds its t-0w value of -8.9 following a WORKPLACES one-week drop steeper than 5 points.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM holding above +40 while RESIDENTIAL stays above +6 shows household spending is concentrated in essentials and home time is elevated; discretionary retail trips stay suppressed and RETAIL_REC remains below its prior 28-day mean.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM weekly mean > 40 and RESIDENTIAL weekly mean > 6 simultaneously
evidence_refs: fact:all four weekly GROCERY_PHARM means exceed 41 and all four RESIDENTIAL means exceed 6
failure_condition: Next-28-day mean RETAIL_REC exceeds the prior 28-day mean while GROCERY_PHARM stays above 40 and RESIDENTIAL above 6.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS stabilised at -17.6 after the -21.9 trough, showing outdoor mobility has stopped deteriorating as the summer outdoor season opens; normalised outdoor activity spills over into retail-and-recreation footfall within two weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS prints two consecutive weekly means at or above -18.0
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not rise above -8.9 over the 14 days after PARKS holds two consecutive weeks at or above -18.0.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL rebounded to +7.6 in the latest week after two weeks at +6.1, showing households retreating home again; each additional point of time at home substitutes directly away from retail-and-recreation trips in the following week.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL rose from +6.1 at t-1w to +7.6 at t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises in the week after a RESIDENTIAL week-on-week increase greater than 1.0 point.

mechanism_narrative: Conditional on the reopening gate being open (TRANSIT above -10 and PARKS above -20), recovering transit ridership is the leading channel that pulls discretionary trips back; the gate is satisfied at t-0w so RETAIL_REC should climb over four weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT weekly mean > -10.0 and PARKS weekly mean > -20.0
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT -7.4 and PARKS -17.6 satisfy the reopening gate at t-0w
regime_hint: reopening gate open (TRANSIT above -10, PARKS above -20)
failure_condition: With the reopening gate open, the next-28-day mean RETAIL_REC is at or below the prior 28-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: The mid-June decision point sits at the start of the summer leisure ramp; as school terms end, leisure and recreation trips expand independently of work commuting, lifting RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS deficit narrowed from -21.9 at t-2w to -17.6 at t-0w as the outdoor season began
failure_condition: Next-28-day mean RETAIL_REC is lower than the prior 28-day mean, contradicting the seasonal-lift claim.
